facts.raw_span: A 56-year-old man presented with a 2-month history of bitemporal hemianopia and left labial numbness
visual impairment, bitemporal hemianopia, and right abducens nerve palsy

Pituitary MRI demonstrated diffuse swelling of the pituitary body and stalk, a 7-mm poorly enhancing mass in the right anterior lobe, loss of the posterior pituitary bright spot on T1-weighted images, and thickening of the sphenoid sinus mucosa
Serum IgG4 was elevated at 319 mg/dL
A 56-year-old man presented with a 2-month history of bitemporal hemianopia and left labial numbness
visual impairment, bitemporal hemianopia, and right abducens nerve palsy

Pituitary MRI demonstrated diffuse swelling of the pituitary body and stalk, a 7-mm poorly enhancing mass in the right anterior lobe, loss of the posterior pituitary bright spot on T1-weighted images, and thickening of the sphenoid sinus mucosa
Serum IgG4 was elevated at 319 mg/dL

concepts.why: The patient's elevated IgG4 levels, hypopituitarism, and pituitary MRI findings are consistent with IgG4-related hypophysitis.
The patient's hypopituitarism, visual impairment, and pituitary MRI findings could be consistent with lymphocytic hypophysitis.
The 7-mm poorly enhancing mass in the right anterior lobe of the pituitary gland could be a pituitary adenoma.
The patient's hypopituitarism, visual impairment, and elevated IgG4 levels could be consistent with granulomatosis with polyangiitis.
The patient's hypopituitarism, visual impairment, and elevated IgG4 levels could be consistent with sarcoidosis.
The patient's hypopituitarism, visual impairment, and pituitary MRI findings could be consistent with tubercular hypophysitis.
The patient's elevated IgG4 levels and systemic findings are consistent with IgG4-related disease.
The patient's pituitary MRI findings could be consistent with pituitary apoplexy.

rationales.F06: Low LH levels suggest hypopituitarism, which is consistent with IgG4-related hypophysitis and lymphocytic hypophysitis.
rationales.F07: Low FSH levels suggest hypopituitarism, which is consistent with IgG4-related hypophysitis and lymphocytic hypophysitis.
rationales.F11: Pituitary MRI findings are consistent with IgG4-related hypophysitis, and the loss of the posterior pituitary bright spot on T1-weighted images suggests hypophysitis.
rationales.F12: Elevated IgG4 levels are a key diagnostic feature of IgG4-related disease, including IgG4-related hypophysitis.

frontier_selector.rationale: Elevated IgG4 levels, diffuse swelling of the pituitary body and stalk, and thickening of the sphenoid sinus mucosa support IgG4-related hypophysitis, with lymphocytic hypophysitis as a less specific alternative due to similar MRI findings but without elevated IgG4 levels.
